title: Report early public Mindless endings without claiming five completed minutes

source.ref: DAWN and Frequency render tests reproduced the same false completed-duration claim after a twelve-second session, 2026-10-24

detail: Both public timer designs mapped End early to the same outcome as a full five-minute session, always claiming Five minutes, done. Completion now records whether the wall-clock deadline was reached: a partial session says Session ended, natural completion keeps the five-minute outcome, and a stop after a throttled interval has crossed the deadline is correctly complete. The Frequency partial outcome uses the existing side tone. Retry resets the clock and the free-account link remains wired. Corrected pre-repair fixtures reproduced four app failures across completion and paused animation; an initial generic fake-timer count also saw Next Link prefetch work, so the clock tests isolate link navigation while retaining destination assertions. The related timer/movement/setup/recovery/action batch passes 188 tests in 15 files. Seven assertion-level controls across completion and animation fail as intended. Real React browser fixtures verify early stop, accelerated natural completion, retry and zero remaining session intervals for DAWN and Frequency; phone/desktop and dark/Stage contexts have no measured horizontal overflow. The first Frequency fixture omitted its marketing Stage attribute; it was corrected from the canonical shell before final captures. These are local component fixtures with anchor navigation and combined preview CSS, not deployed/full-route or authenticated acceptance. No production data, logs, rewards or provider sends are exercised. Whole-tree integration of this later repair remains pending.

verify.note: Run actual DAWN/Frequency React components against local DOM and clock recorders, including partial, natural and throttled-deadline completion, retry/link and interval cleanup; no backend.
